g-a-kolbe-of-piet-retief.v: almost certainly GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE, the Settler's twin son
g-a-kolbe-of-piet-retief.r: A DATE FOR THE TWIN, IF IT IS HIM. The stone at PIET RETIEF reads “VADER EN MOEDER — G.A. KOLBE — GEB. 23 FEB. 1836 — OVERL. 7 JAN. 1913 — A.M. KOLBE — GEB. 4 MEI 1843 — OVERL. 21 SEP. 1907 — VAN HUN KINDERS”. The Settler's ninth and tenth children were TWINS born at BURGERSDORP IN 1836, Charlotte Felicia and George Augustus, and this archive has never had a day for either. A G.A. KOLBE BORN 23 FEBRUARY 1836 IS EXACTLY THE RIGHT MAN IN EXACTLY THE RIGHT YEAR — and it would date his twin sister too. IT IS INITIALS AND A YEAR, NOT A NAME AND A PARENT, and this archive has spent today being careful about exactly this. john-gerson-eliezar-kolbe.v: “Jan” · JOHN GERSON ELIEZER KOLBE, in his obituary · Commandant Kolbe
john-gerson-eliezar-kolbe.r: THE SETTLER'S ELDEST CHILD, AND UNTIL TODAY A LINE IN A TABLE. His obituary — Grahamstown Journal, 15 April 1868, headed “DEATH OF COMMANDANT KOLBE” — gives the whole man. Born 7 JULY 1822; married 3 APRIL 1843 to ANNA JACOBA VAN DER MERWE; DIED 3 APRIL 1868, ON HIS WEDDING ANNIVERSARY, at the farm LEEUWBERG, of TYPHUS OR TYPHOID CAUGHT ON COMMANDO — “thus adding another to the long list of victims of our miserable war”. He had settled on KAALSPRUIT about 1850 and lies there — AND HE CONFIRMS THE FARM HIMSELF. A lost-property advertisement he placed in the Friend on 9 MARCH 1864 is signed “J.G.E. KOLBE, Kafferberg, Kaalspruit” (the address as the paper printed it). The Friend’s own obituary transcription reads “[Randspruit]”, bracketed by the transcriber as doubtful; the man’s own address settles it. THAT ADVERTISEMENT ALSO PUTS THE TWO BROTHERS IN ONE DOCUMENT: it concerns “a promissory note, date 9th March 1864, drawn by GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE in favor of J.G.E. KOLBE, payable 4 months after date for £154 Stg” — lost on the Market Square at Bloemfontein. HE LEFT A WIDOW AND TWELVE CHILDREN — “OF THE EIGHT SONS AND FOUR DAUGHTERS HE HAS LEFT BEHIND HIM”, which is the Friend of the Free State’s own wording and a count the Grahamstown reprint drops. Only one daughter was married and the youngest child was an infant; TWO SONS HAD BEEN SERVING WITH HIM IN THE FIELD and “proved themselves amongst the bravest of our burghers”. NONE OF THE TWELVE IS NAMED AND NONE IS IN THIS ARCHIVE. He was COMMANDANT OF THE DISTRICT, A JUSTICE OF THE PEACE, A DIRECTOR OF THE BLOEMFONTEIN BANK and a DEACON of the Dutch Reformed Church, and he had spoken in the VOLKSRAAD in May 1867. He had refused public life for twelve years after THE ABANDONMENT, having protested the British withdrawal and applied to SIR GEORGE CLERK for compensation for his land so that he might leave with the troops; failing that, “he, like many more, had to cast his lot with the Free State”. AND ON HIS DEATHBED, in full possession of his senses, he told the doctor and the others present THAT THIS STATE HAD TAKEN TOO MUCH LAND FROM THE BASUTOS, that he had always thought so and had said so in the Raad, and begged them to rescind the resolution and treat with the Governor for an equitable boundary. 20 SEPTEMBER 2026 — A HISTORIAN’S DRAFT NAMES HIM TOO, AND NAMES THE WAR. The DSAB entry on his father says the eldest son “J.G.E. KOLBE (1822–68), was later op LEEUBERG naby Bloemfontein woonagtig en het gedurende die TWEEDE SOTHO-VRYSTAATOORLOG roem verwerf as KOMMANDANT”. BOTH YEARS MATCH THIS ARCHIVE TO THE YEAR — born 7 July 1822, dead 3 April 1868 — and both were got from an obituary and an auction advertisement that the entry does not cite. It is the strongest of the nine places where that entry and this archive agree from different documents. AND IT NAMES WHAT KILLED HIM: the obituary said only “our miserable war”; the war was the SECOND SOTHO–FREE STATE WAR. AND HE MAY BE IN THE 1830 LETTER, AGED EIGHT. Read from the file rather than from a mail preview, MSB 751 encloses “a Jacket & waistcoat FOR JOHN & a further Jacket also for him, tell him HIS OLD FATHER has sent it him, & TO MAKE HASTE TO FILL THEM OUT”. CLOTHES FOR A GROWING CHILD, sent from Soho to the Cape in August 1830, when this man was eight years old and the eldest son of the house. IF IT IS HIM IT IS THE EARLIEST DOCUMENT IN THIS ARCHIVE THAT MENTIONS HIM. “His old father” is the difficulty and is not glossed over — the writer is his GRANDFATHER, and this is an inference, not a reading.

francis-mccabe.r: THE SECOND HUSBAND, and the reason the Commandant's widow is filed under the wrong surname in the Free State estate index. LANDDROST OF BLOEMFONTEIN, son of DR PATRICK McCABE, a Staff-Assistant Surgeon attached to the British Army on the Cape Frontier; his mother ROSE died at Bloemfontein on 1 August 1858, aged 72 years 3 months and 8 days. He married Anna Jacoba van der Merwe about APRIL 1871 — “his second wife, about ten months since” — and was dead within fifteen months. ON THE ANNIVERSARY OF THE STATE'S INDEPENDENCE he had spent the day superintending the burghers' annual target shooting for the government prize; at a quarter past five he set off by spring-cart for the Diamond Fields meaning to sleep at his own farm “UITVLUGT” on the Modder River; at about half past seven, in deceptive moonlight and one hour's ride short of the farm of G.F. Enslin, the cart went into a sluit washed out by the rains. He was dead of heart disease that evening. HE LEFT FOUR SONS AND TWO DAUGHTERS OF HIS OWN AND “A LARGE FAMILY OF STEP-CHILDREN”, which is a newspaper counting the Commandant's twelve. His brother JOSEPH, the well-known trader and traveller, had died in the interior in December 1865; his brother JOHN died at Bloemfontein in 1860. He was buried on the Sunday afternoon at six o'clock, the coffin carried by the resident members of the Volksraad and the principal government officers, with the State President and upwards of two hundred walking behind. 15 SEPTEMBER, FROM THE FREE STATE ESTATE INDEX. VAB MHG C129: “MCCABE, FRANCIS. EGGENOTES 1) MARIA PETRONELLA ELISABETHA ANTOINETTA RAATH EN 2) ANNA (GEBORE VAN DER MERWE)”, 1872 — SO HE HAD A FIRST WIFE AND SHE HAS A NAME. And VAB 1/3/1/12 BC11: “MCCABE, FRANCIS. INSOLVENTE BOEDEL”, with the remark “BEVAT GEEN STERFKENNIS NIE” — CONTAINS NO DEATH NOTICE. The Landdrost of Bloemfontein, buried with the State President walking behind him and two hundred people after that, LEFT AN INSOLVENT ESTATE. His widow's own entry, M777, names both her husbands, so the remarriage is in the archives and not only in a newspaper.

The Free State criminal court, October 1868: a horse thief drove off three animals from the farm SPRINGFIELD, ward Upper Modder-river, district Bloemfontein — a black mare and foal belonging to “ANNA JACOBA VAN DER MERWE, WIDOW OF LATE J.G.E. KOLBE”, a blue schimmel mare and foal belonging to “JOHN KOLBE, JUN.”, and a chestnut riding horse belonging to a man named Jephts. SIX MONTHS AFTER HIS FATHER DIED HE IS HOLDING STOCK IN HIS OWN RIGHT BESIDE HIS MOTHER. He is named by initial and suffix only, and nothing else about him is known — but AN EIGHTH OF THE OBITUARY'S “EIGHT SONS” NOW HAS A DOCUMENT. In 1884 The Friend reported that the eldest son of “Mr. John KOLBE”, a boy of ten called LITTLE JANNIE, was struck dead by lightning on his father's farm five hours north of Bloemfontein; the Natal Witness index carries the same death and names the father GEORGE. Two papers, two fathers, and this archive will not choose.

anna-jacoba-van-der-merwe.r: SHE REMARRIED, AND HER SECOND HUSBAND IS WHY SHE WAS HARD TO FIND. The Free State archives hold her under a different surname: VAB MHG M777 — “MCCABE, ANNA JACOBA. NOOIENSVAN VAN DER MERWE. EGGENOTE JOHN GHERSON [KOLBE]”, 1896. WIDOWED IN 1868 WITH TWELVE CHILDREN AND DEAD TWENTY-EIGHT YEARS LATER AS MRS MCCABE. Her husband’s own estate is beside it — VAB MHG K71, “KOLBE, JOHN GERSON ELEAZAR. EGGENOTE ANNA JACOBA (GEBORE VAN DER MERWE)”, 1868. AND THE McCABE NAME IS ALREADY IN THIS ARCHIVE: a ROSA MAGDALENA KOLBE was baptised at Bloemfontein in 1890 to Frederik Fortuna Kolbe and MARIA PETRONELLA ELIZABETH ANTOINETTA MCCABE — a second Kolbe–McCabe marriage in the same small Free State world, and this archive does not yet know whether that is a coincidence. NEITHER ESTATE IS READ. M777 is the document that would name the twelve children. Married JOHN GERSON ELIEZAR KOLBE on 3 APRIL 1843 and was widowed on the same date twenty-five years later. She is the third van der Merwe to marry into these families. 15 SEPTEMBER 2026 — McCABE HAS A FIRST NAME, A BIRTH DATE AND AN OFFICE. He is FRANCIS McCABE, LANDDROST OF BLOEMFONTEIN, son of Dr Patrick McCabe, a Staff-Assistant Surgeon attached to the British Army on the Cape Frontier, born at one of the military posts in what is now British Kaffraria on 29 SEPTEMBER 1817. His obituary in The Friend says he “married his second wife about ten months since — THE WIDOW OF THE LATE COMMANDANT J.G.E. KOLBE, OF KAFIRBERG, NEAR THIS TOWN”, and he died suddenly of heart disease on the Modder River road on 23 FEBRUARY 1872, aged 54, leaving “a widow, four sons and two daughters, BESIDES A LARGE FAMILY OF STEP-CHILDREN”. SO: MARRIED 3 APRIL 1843, WIDOWED 3 APRIL 1868 WITH TWELVE CHILDREN, MARRIED AGAIN ABOUT APRIL 1871, WIDOWED AGAIN FIFTEEN MONTHS LATER, AND DEAD IN 1896 UNDER HIS NAME. For about eleven months there were eighteen children attached to one household. She was living at SPRINGFIELD, WARD UPPER MODDER-RIVER, DISTRICT BLOEMFONTEIN in October 1868, when a black mare and foal of hers were stolen — the court record that says so is the only document this archive has that shows her doing anything at all.

hits.text: It is not a pedigree. The document that would make it one is VAB MHG M777 , the 1896 estate of the Commandant’s widow Anna Jacoba van der Merwe , filed under her second husband’s name McCabe — which would name all twelve children . It is identified, it is unread, and it is in Bloemfontein. The Commandant → One limit worth stating. FindMyPast’s newspaper archive is British and Irish.

coenraad-johannes-otto-werdmuller.d: 1882 — death notice KAB MOOC 6/9/187, 4160; will MOOC 7/1/431, 102
coenraad-johannes-otto-werdmuller.r: HE IS IN THE CAPE ARCHIVES FROM 1854 TO 1882 AND HE DIED IN 1882, not merely “before February 1884”. Motions in the Supreme Court in 1854, 1855, 1872 and 1873; a trustee in other men’s insolvent estates; and in 1882, GSC 2/1/1/41 no. 60, “CHARLES ANDREW WERDMULLER AND COENRAAD JOHANNES OTTO WERDMULLER TRADING AS C.A. WERDMULLER AND COMPANY” — FATHER AND SON IN BUSINESS TOGETHER, in the year he died. His own death notice and will are both filed and neither is read. THE MAN THE SETTLER’S FOURTH DAUGHTER MARRIED, and until today a bracket after her name. He is at BURGERSDORP in April 1857, standing at a font with AUGUSTA LOUISA KOLBE. He is at Burgersdorp again on 7 JULY 1874, married BY SPECIAL LICENCE by the Rev. William Cromar to ELIZABETH JOHANNA CATHARINE VORSTER — and the Eastern Province Herald prints his name in full as COENRAAD JOHANNES OTTO WERDMULLER D’ELGG, which is the first time this archive has seen the von Elgg written by anyone but a genealogist. He is DEAD by February 1884, when his second son marries as the son of “the late C.J.O. Werdmuller of Burghersdorp”. WHETHER AUGUSTA LOUISA WAS DEAD BEFORE 1874 THIS ARCHIVE DOES NOT KNOW.

charles-andrew-werdmuller.r: THE DATES NOW CLOSE AROUND HIM, THOUGH NO DOCUMENT YET NAMES HIS MOTHER. His father’s first wife, AUGUSTA LOUISA KOLBE, MADE A WILL IN 1868 AND DIED IN 1873 — KAB MOOC 7/1/332 no. 205, “KOLBE, AUGUSTA LOUISA, WIFE OF COENRAAD JOHANNES OTTO WERDMULLER VAN ELGG”, filed 1873 — and his father remarried on 7 JULY 1874. IN 1882 CHARLES ANDREW WAS IN BUSINESS WITH HIS FATHER as C.A. Werdmuller and Company, and in February 1884 he married. A SON OF THE 1874 MARRIAGE WOULD HAVE BEEN SEVEN AND NINE. He can only be a child of the first marriage, and the first wife is the Settler’s daughter. THE ONE LOOPHOLE LEFT is an earlier wife before Augusta Louisa, and his father’s 1882 DEATH NOTICE would close it by naming the children. SECOND SON OF THE LATE C.J.O. WERDMULLER OF BURGHERSDORP, married at Wesley Church, Queenstown, on 13 FEBRUARY 1884 to CHARLOTTE ANNE CALLAGHAN, eldest daughter of Hugh Callaghan of Ashby Manor. Of STEYNSBURG then, and by 1909 CHARLES WERDMULLER, J.P., OF HOOPSTAD in the Orange River Colony — the town his wife died in. HIS MOTHER IS NOT NAMED ON ANYTHING READ HERE. If he is the child born 14 February 1857 at Burgersdorp he is AUGUSTA LOUISA KOLBE’S SON and a grandson of the 1820 Settler; if he belongs to his father’s 1874 marriage he is no relation at all, and a man marrying in 1884 as a second son cannot be. augusta-louisa-kolbe.r: THE SETTLER'S FOURTH DAUGHTER HAS THREE DOCUMENTS AND THIS ARCHIVE HAD NONE OF THEM. A WILL, MADE IN 1868 AND FILED IN 1873: KAB MOOC 7/1/332 no. 205, “KOLBE, AUGUSTA LOUISA. WIFE OF COENRAAD JOHANNES OTTO WERDMULLER VAN ELGG” — which is the first document read here that ties her to that man by anything but a newspaper. A DEATH NOTICE, MOOC 6/9/145 no. 9981, 1873. And a LIQUIDATION AND DISTRIBUTION ACCOUNT, MOOC 13/1/299 no. 93, 1874, which means there was something to distribute. SHE DIED IN 1873 AND HER HUSBAND REMARRIED IN JULY 1874 — a year and a month, which is what a widower does, and which settles the question this archive left open yesterday about whose son Charles Andrew is. NONE OF THE THREE IS READ.

frederick-fortunatus-werdmuller.r: THE FORTUNATUS NAME IN A FOURTH SURNAME. “PETITION OF FREDERICK FORTUNATUS WERDMULLER OF MALMESBURY”, Cape Supreme Court, 1907, twice in one year, both times in other men's insolvent estates; and an estate of his own in 1953. This archive has already followed FREDERIK FORTUNATUS from Kolbe (1839) to Barry (1863) to Booÿsen (1899); here it is again, on a Werdmuller — and Augusta Louisa Kolbe married a Werdmuller. 17 SEPTEMBER 2026 — HE IS SHOWN TO BE HER SON, AND THE SENTENCE ABOVE IS WITHDRAWN. The last 214 images of the Burgersdorp baptism register hold his font: FREDRIK FORTUNATUS STEENKAMP WERDMULLER, BORN 25 APRIL 1861, BAPTISED 19 MAY 1861 AT BURGERSDORP, FATHER COENRAAD JOHANNES OTTO WERDMULLER, MOTHER AUGUSTA LOUISA KOLBE — FamilySearch 1:1:6FW6-WXGS, image 673. THE SETTLER’S FOURTH DAUGHTER GAVE HER CHILD HER BROTHER’S NAME, which is how Frederik Fortunatus reached a fourth surname. AND IT DATES AUGUSTA LOUISA: she was bearing her husband’s children in 1861, thirteen years before he married again at Burgersdorp in 1874 — which bears directly on whether Charles Andrew was her son. THE ONE STEP NOT TAKEN: that the child of 1861 is the man of the 1907 petition and the 1953 estate. Both are Frederick Fortunatus Werdmuller at the Cape and the name is rare; the 1907 man is of MALMESBURY and the child was baptised at BURGERSDORP, and no document read here joins them.

charlotte-anne-callaghan.r: ELDEST DAUGHTER OF HUGH CALLAGHAN, ESQ., OF ASHBY MANOR, district of Queenstown; married Charles Andrew Werdmuller on 13 February 1884. SEVEN YEARS LATER SHE WAS DEAD AT THIRTY-TWO, at Hoopstad, “after a long illness”, and a correspondent’s obituary in the Queenstown Free Press adds that she had arrived there only a few months before, in indifferent health, with a disorder of the heart that proved organic. SHE LEFT “A HUSBAND AND TWO LITTLE GIRLS”, and it is that line which lets the 1909 marriage notice call Amy a second daughter.

hits.title: What changed
hits.text: The route is closed for a demonstrable reason, and what remains is the registers themselves, read across the gaps. Two fonts, a year apart, and every witness a Kolbe Found found Having read one Barry baptism, the one before it was worth reading too. At the 1847 font the witnesses are John Kolbe, Margaret Kolbe and Augusta Kolbe; at the 1848 font, Catharine Sophia Maria Kolbe. Two children, two years, and not a Barry witness between them. That is the same conclusion the namesake correction reached from one entry, arrived at a second time from another — the names this archive has called Barry names belong to the people who stood at the fonts, and they were all Kolbes.

catharine-sophia-maria-kolbe.v: Catharine Kolbe (1853) · Catharine Sophia Maria Kolber (1848)
catharine-sophia-maria-kolbe.r: SHE IS WHERE THE NAME COMES FROM, and this archive had her down as “Catharine Kolbe” and nothing more. On 13 November 1848 she stood godmother at Graaff-Reinet to her sister Margaretha's son HENRY JAMES BARRY, entry 603, and the clerk wrote her out in full: CATHARINE SOPHIA MARIA KOLBER. ELEVEN YEARS LATER her sister named a daughter CATHERINE MARIA SOPHIA — the Kathleen Barry who married into this family — and the name then ran through four more generations and three more surnames. This archive had called it a Barry name. It is a Kolbe name, and it belongs to a woman who never married into the Booyzens at all. She is also godmother at Burgersdorp in 1853, two entries above her sister Mary Elizabeth's son.

mary-elizabeth-kolbe.r: HER DEATH IS NOW DATED, AND SHE DIED WITHOUT A WILL. The Friend of the Free State, 23 October 1863, twice in two weeks: “Derwyl MARIA ELIZABETH KOLBE zonder testament na te laten is overleden en de nagebleven echtgenoot G.F. ENSLIN by brieve van administratie ter vereffening van haren boedel als executeur is aangesteld” — she had died INTESTATE and her husband was appointed executor of her estate. This archive had only “before 1867”, inferred. It is now BEFORE 23 OCTOBER 1863, from a notice her own husband placed. MARGARETHA'S SISTER, and the woman who married GEORGE FREDERICK ENSLIN — which is the whole answer to a contradiction this archive carried as Serious, that Margaretha appeared to marry Enslin while married to John Barry. It was resolved from Margaret Downing's 1867 death notice. The Burgersdorp register of 23 October 1853 shows it instead: the two sisters baptising a son each, two entries apart, on one page.

william-barry.r: Found twice in one day. He came in on the 1915 death notice of his mother Margaretha Kolbe, estate 1291, which names NINE children where his father's names eight — and then the Burgersdorp doopregister produced his baptism: WILLIAM FREDRIK, born 23 August 1853, christened 23 October, godparents JOHN KOLBE, ANNA VAN DER MERWE and GEORGE KOLBE. Two of the three are his mother's brothers. A SECOND William Frederick Thomas was baptised in 1861 and this archive cannot say whether the first died or a clerk erred — a doubt re-surfaced, and briefly mistaken for a new find, when the index was asked for every Barry child of a Kolbe mother. He is not on his father's notice, not on the Cape Rebel roll, and nowhere else in this archive. His father's 1903 registration said ELEVEN children; with William there are nine named and two still missing.

alida-jacoba-van-ellinckhuizen.r: Wife of John Augustus Barry II and the mother of nine children baptised at Burgersdorp and Dordrecht between 1871 and 1889. This archive had John Augustus II as a name on two death notices with no wife and no children at all until the index was asked for every Barry child of a father called John Augustus. Her surname is spelled nine different ways across the entries — Ellinckhuizen, Ellinckhuisen, Elinchhiusen, Westerhuizen, Ellincahuyzen — and one son carries it as a forename. FROM THE INDEX.

He remains exactly what he was: an unresolved second William, indexed twice over to Graaff-Reinet and Dordrecht , eight years after the Burgersdorp baptism . On Henry Jaonas there is an argument, and it comes entirely out of figures this archive already held. John Augustus Barry II was born 13 March 1847 and baptised four weeks later — a documented date, off a register. James Henry Barry is carried in this archive as born "about 1847" , and that figure is not a register at all: it is an age worked back from his death at Barkly East on 23 June 1939. Two brothers cannot both be born in 1847 , and the approximate date is the one that has to give way.

johan-gottlieb-kolbe.v: John Gottlob · “JOHN GODLOFF KOLBE ESQ. OF BRUNSWICK-SQUARE”, in his son’s 1844 obituary · and twenty-four spellings in the Westminster rate books
johan-gottlieb-kolbe.tree: The 1844 obituary’s “Brunswick-square”. No Westminster rate book, land tax return, census or burial register places him there, and Bloomsbury’s own sources have not been searched.
johan-gottlieb-kolbe.r: HE HAD EIGHT SONS, AND THIS ARCHIVE KNEW OF ONE. His son’s obituary in the Grahamstown Journal of 19 December 1844 calls George Augustus “THE LAST REMAINING OF EIGHT SONS OF JOHN GODLOFF KOLBE ESQ. OF BRUNSWICK-SQUARE, LONDON”. SEVEN BROTHERS, ALL DEAD BEFORE DECEMBER 1844, none of them named anywhere in this archive — and dead men do not appear in a census, which is why the 1841 Conduit Street household holds three women and no sons. THE OBITUARY ALSO PUTS HIM AT BRUNSWICK SQUARE, in Bloomsbury, where the census and the death put him at CONDUIT STREET in Mayfair, a mile and a half away. Both can be true twenty years apart, and this archive has already moved this man once — off the family tree’s Lamb’s Conduit Street — so it records a second address rather than making a second correction. “ESQ.”, not “tailor”. AND HE IS IN THE LONDON GAZETTE, nine years before he died: issue 19424, page 1702, 29 September 1836, dissolving the copartnership of “JOHN GOTTLOB KOLBE and DAVID FLETCHER, of Conduit-Street, Bond-Street, in the County of Middlesex, TAILORS”. That is his trade, his street and a business partner, in print, from a free source — and it pushes him back to Conduit Street in 1836. AND THE DEATH IS NOW A GRO REFERENCE: FreeBMD gives one Kolbe death in all of England and Wales for 1845–46 — “Deaths Dec 1845, KOLBE, JOHN GOTTLOB, ST GEO HAN SQ, VOL 1, PAGE 35”. The district matches the census; the name form JOHN GOTTLOB matches his son's 1803 baptism; and the certificate, not yet ordered, would name the informant. FOUND IN THE 1841 CENSUS, which settles two things this archive had argued from other documents. He is at CONDUIT STREET, St George Hanover Square, sub-district MAY FAIR, aged 76 — four years before he died at number 34, and independent of the death record that corrected the family tree's Lamb's Conduit Street. And his birth county is entered as “FOREIGN”, which is the first document in this archive to say in its own words that he was not English. HO107, piece 734, book 1, folio 11, page 15, SCHEDULE 38. Three women share that schedule: Marianne, 35, Charlotte, 30, and Amelia A., 25. Tailor. Died at 34 Conduit Street, Mayfair — not Lamb's Conduit Street; the tree's photograph is of the wrong building. 16 SEPTEMBER 2026 — THE ADDRESS ARGUMENT IS OVER, AND HE HAD TWO WIVES. The WESTMINSTER RATE BOOKS index him ONE HUNDRED AND TWENTY-ONE TIMES between 1800 and 1831, under TWENTY-FOUR SPELLINGS of his forename — Gothel, Gotleb, Gotleib, Gotlieb, Gotliel, Gotlob, Gotlobe, Goltief, Gottieb, Gottiel, Gottlieb, Gottlob, Gutlieb, Kottieb, Gilliet and once “Jos Gottiel”. In 1800 he is at BROAD STREET NORTH, St James Piccadilly, folio 41 — which independently corroborates the printed 1799 list of 234 master tailors, “Kolbe, John, 18 Broad-street, Soho”. From 1811 to 1831 he is at CHURCH STREET SOUTH, ST ANNE’S SOHO, year after year, and the 1829 land tax return says the same. BRUNSWICK SQUARE APPEARS IN NO RATE BOOK, NO LAND TAX RETURN, NO CENSUS AND NO BURIAL REGISTER — those are Westminster sources and Bloomsbury would not be in them, so they cannot disprove it, but Soho 1800–1831, St George Hanover Square in 1841 and a death there in 1845 leaves no window for it. AND THE BURIAL IS NOW A REGISTER ENTRY RATHER THAN A TREE CLAIM: Westminster Burials, City of Westminster Archives Centre — DIED 18 NOVEMBER 1845, BURIED 26 NOVEMBER 1845 AT ST JOHN THE BAPTIST, GREAT MARLBOROUGH STREET, page 7, year of birth given as 1764. The date matches the tree’s “26 November 1845, entry 55, grave 7” to the day and the “7” matches; the church does not. 20 SEPTEMBER 2026 — HE WRITES, AND HE SIGNS HIMSELF. MSB 751 at the National Library of South Africa is a letter of FOUR SIDES headed “LONDON AUGUST 23. 1830”, opening “DEAR GEORGE” and signed “YOUR AFFECTIONATE FATHER, J G KOLBE”. IT IS THE FIRST DOCUMENT IN THIS ARCHIVE HE WROTE HIMSELF — everything else is somebody writing about him. IT DOES NOT CARRY A STREET ADDRESS: the heading is “London” and nothing finer, so it does NOT settle Brunswick Square against Conduit Street, which is what this archive most hoped for. WHAT IT DOES CARRY: his son’s acceptance by the LONDON MISSIONARY SOCIETY in the father’s own words, DR PHILIP carrying an earlier letter to the Cape, MR MILES of the Society calling at the house, HENRY dying of DROPSY and “resigned to the Catastrophe”, MILNE AND ELIZABETH — “Betsey” — removed to EDINBURGH, CHARLOTTE sending an Evangelical Magazine, a SUIT OF BLACK CLOTHES sent out for a newly accepted missionary, the death of George IV and the French revolution of July 1830 as fresh news, and a request that his son fact-check a baboon story in a magazine. AND THE LINE THAT COUNTS MOST: “KIND LOVE FROM YOUR SISTERS & BROTHER” — SISTERS PLURAL, BROTHER SINGULAR. Of the eight sons, two were alive in August 1830. 20 SEPTEMBER, READ AGAIN FROM THE FILE INSTEAD OF FROM A MAIL PREVIEW, AND IT CARRIES MORE. DR PHILIP IS NOT JUST THE COURIER — “Dr Philip was exceedingly glad to hear of you being accepted by the L.M.S. as you may well imagine, HE HAS PROMISED TO WRITE TO YOU A LETTER BY THE FIRST OPPORTUNITY”. HE SENDS A BOX: a suit of black clothes for George, and a jacket and waistcoat FOR JOHN with a further jacket, “tell him his old father has sent it him, & to make haste to fill them out”. A YEAR OF NEWSPAPERS, one number lost by Henry. AND THE HOUSE HAS FRIENDS WITH NAMES, the first in this archive who simply knew them: MR & MRS STANHOPE, MR AND MRS WARNER, and MRS FIELD AND HER DAUGHTERS — “the eldest, Miss Mary, that was, HAS MARRIED A MR BELLEW, A SURGEON”. TWO OF HIS FOUR PAGES GO ON A STORY FROM THE MIRROR about a Scottish colonist near the Xhosa whose wife was carried off by orang-outangs and recovered after two years as their queen — AND HE DOES NOT BELIEVE A WORD OF IT: “here we look upon the Story as a fictious & romance… I should be glad to hear from you, WHETHER THAT REPORT MAY BE FOUNDED IN TRUTH, OR FALSEHOOD.” A tailor of seventy, reading a cheap weekly, writing to the one man he knew who was actually there to ask whether it was true. HIS FIRST WIFE MARY DIED 2 AUGUST 1814 AGED 46 and his SECOND, ALSO MARY, DIED 15 AUGUST 1824 AGED 36, both buried in the German Lutheran Church register, TNA RG 4/4631 — which is why one Mary could never be made to fit a run of baptisms from 1792 to 1819. AND THE LONDON GAZETTE HOLDS FIVE NOTICES, NOT THE ONE THIS ARCHIVE HAD. 12 MAY 1824 — the partnership of JOHN GOTLOB KOLBE AND JOHN HENRY KOLBE, of CHURCH-STREET, SOHO, TAILORS, dissolved. 30 SEPTEMBER 1836 — Kolbe and DAVID FLETCHER of Conduit-Street dissolved. 21 MARCH 1845 — “JOHN GOTLIEB KOLBE AND RICHARD DAVIES, OF CONDUIT-STREET, BOND-STREET, TAILORS, HAS BEEN DISSOLVED BY MUTUAL CONSENT”, EIGHT MONTHS BEFORE HE DIED and still calling himself a tailor, which is what the obituary’s “Esq. of Brunswick-square” has to be set against. 1824 WAS THE YEAR IT ALL WENT: the partnership dissolved in May, his second wife dead in August, and his son in the insolvent debtors’ lists in October and November. 16 SEPTEMBER, LATER — AND THE 1799 TAILORS’ LIST HAS A TWIN. In APRIL AND MAY 1834 the London press printed the roll of “considerably more than THREE HUNDRED of the Master Tailors of the metropolis” who met at Willis’s Rooms, St James’s-street, to resist THE GRAND NATIONAL CONSOLIDATED TRADES’ UNION, and the entry reads “KOLBE AND FLETCHER, CONDUIT-STREET” — Morning Post 30 April, Globe 30 April and 10 May, Old England 4 May, Morning Herald 10 May, London Courier 10 May, True Sun 10 May, Public Ledger 12 May. SEVEN NEWSPAPERS, ONE LINE. 20 SEPTEMBER 2026 — AND A HISTORIAN CALLED HIM AN APOTHECARY. The DSAB draft entry on his son opens “die seun van J.G.Kolbe, ’n DUITSE APTEKER wat in Londen woonagtig was”. THE GERMAN IS RIGHT AND THE LONDON IS RIGHT AND THE TRADE IS HIS SON’S — George Augustus sailed in 1820 as an apothecary, and the apothecary has been handed back up to the father. IT IS THE ONLY THING IN THAT ENTRY THIS ARCHIVE CAN SHOW TO BE WRONG, and it can only show it because it read the rate books. IT CLOSES THE GAP: the rate books had him in Soho to 1831 and the Gazette at Conduit Street by 1836; HE WAS AT CONDUIT STREET, WITH FLETCHER, BY 29 APRIL 1834. AND IT RHYMES WITH THE FIRST LIST THIRTY-FIVE YEARS EARLIER — in December 1799 one of 234 masters over the Combination Acts, a young man at 18 Broad-street; in April 1834 a firm with a partner and a Bond Street address, seventy years old, on the masters’ side of the same argument.

charles-kolbe.r: ONE OF THE EIGHT SONS, NAMED FOR THE FIRST TIME. Father John, mother Mary. Batch C15051-2. HIS DEATH IS NOT IN THE GERMAN LUTHERAN REGISTER, which holds six other Kolbe burials — but a second son was christened CHARLES Samuel nine years later, and families reused a name when the first child carrying it had died. That is an inference and not a record.
charles-kolbe.tree: That he died before 1807. It rests on the reuse of the name, not on a burial entry.

john-henry-kolbe.d: 13 Apr 1832, buried 22 Apr 1832, German Lutheran Church
john-henry-kolbe.r: ONE OF THE EIGHT SONS, AND THE ONE WHO LIVED LONGEST OF THOSE FOUND. Baptised 29 July 1800, father John, mother Mary, batch I02559-1. TNA RG 4/4631 folio 100: died 13 April 1832, buried 22 April, AGED 32 — twelve years before the obituary that counted him among the seven already gone. AND HE SPEAKS. Old Bailey, session of 13 January 1819, trial t18190113-149 — Richard Kerr indicted for stealing “one coat, value 6l., the property of JOHN HENRY KOLBE”. His own deposition: “MY FATHER IS A TAILOR, AND LIVES IN CHURCH-STREET, SOHO. On the 9th of January, about eleven o’clock at night, I stopped at the Star and Crown public-house, Westminster, and left my coat over my horse’s head — I had a chaise standing at the door; I saw the prisoner go out, and suspected him — I went out, and missed my coat.” NOT GUILTY. HE WAS EIGHTEEN, and his brother George Augustus sailed for Algoa Bay the following year. It is the only voice this archive has from the Soho house, and it corroborates the rate books’ address from a source that had no interest in it. AND THE LONDON GAZETTE SAYS WHAT BECAME OF HIM. 12 MAY 1824, issue 18027 page 796: the partnership of “JOHN GOTLOB KOLBE AND JOHN HENRY KOLBE, OF CHURCH-STREET, SOHO, IN THE COUNTY OF MIDDLESEX, TAILORS” dissolved — father and son, in business together, at the address he gave the court five years earlier. Then 9 OCTOBER and 16 NOVEMBER 1824, issues 18069 page 1668 and 18080 page 1900, in the INSOLVENT DEBTORS lists, petitions to be heard at Portugal-Street, Lincoln’s-Inn Fields on 5 November: “KOLBE, JOHN HENRY (SUED AS HENRY KOLBE), FORMERLY OF NO. 22, NORFOLK-STREET, MIDDLESEX-HOSPITAL, AND LATE OF NO. 4, MANSFIELD-PLACE”. HE WAS TWENTY-FOUR, OUT OF THE FAMILY BUSINESS AND OUT OF SOHO IN THE SAME YEAR HIS STEPMOTHER DIED, and he was dead at thirty-two. 20 SEPTEMBER 2026 — AND HIS FATHER WRITES ABOUT HIS DYING. MSB 751, the letter of 23 August 1830 to his brother at the Cape: “HENRY had wrote to you himself & left his letter at the Mission house to be forwarded to you… he keeps up pretty well at present, but what effect the winter may have upon him if it should set in very cold, as it did last winter, is perhaps not doubtful, since it must prevent him from taking exercise by walking, & which is a great means of keeping down THE DROPSY, OF WHICH HE BEARS STILL THE SYMPTOMS… I trust also that you will join your prayers, that he may vouchsafe to prepare him to a fit state of meeting his God… HE APPEARS AT PRESENT TO BE RESIGNED TO THE CATASTROPHE.” HE HAD TWENTY MONTHS LEFT. And the same letter’s closing — “kind love from your SISTERS & BROTHER” — makes him THE LAST OF THE EIGHT SONS ALIVE BESIDES GEORGE AUGUSTUS, so that the obituary’s “last remaining of eight sons” became true on 13 April 1832, twelve years before it was printed. AND HE MARRIED THREE MONTHS AFTER THE TRIAL: Westminster Marriages — JOHN HENRY KOLBE AND MATILDA FORD, 26 APRIL 1819, ST MARGARET WESTMINSTER, both of that parish. He was eighteen. A MARY ANN MARIA FORD KOLBE MARRIED AT WHITECHAPEL IN THE FIRST QUARTER OF 1847 — GRO index volume AZ, 840, page 16 — and “Ford” carried as a forename is how families carried a mother’s maiden name. SHE IS VERY PROBABLY HIS DAUGHTER. AND THE PRESS GIVES HIS TRADE, WHICH THE GAZETTE DID NOT. Law Chronicle, Commercial and Bankruptcy Register, 13 January 1825: “KOLBE John Henry, of Norfolk-street, Middlesex-hospital, LAST OF MANSFIELD-ST., KENTISH TOWN, TAILOR, DRAPER” — so he set up on his own account in his father’s trade, and the Gazette’s “Mansfield-Place” is Mansfield Street, Kentish Town. THE MAY 1824 DISSOLUTION WAS REPORTED IN AT LEAST SIX LONDON PAPERS, all of them putting HIS name first: “J. H. Kolbe and J. G. Kolbe, Church-street, Soho, tailors”. AND THE 1830 LETTER SHOWS HIM DOING AN ORDINARY THING. Packing a year of newspapers for the Cape, his father notes one number missing — “the one of the 4th of Decr last, which cannot be found, supposing that HENRY, WHO HAS THEM EVERY WEEK, AFTER I HAVE DONE WITH THEM, — has lost”. The father read the paper first and the son had it after. IT IS THE ONLY DESCRIPTION THIS ARCHIVE HAS OF WHAT ANYBODY IN THAT HOUSE DID WITH AN ORDINARY EVENING, and he had four months to live when it was written.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: This is John Henry Kolbe , baptised at Westminster on 29 July 1800. This archive has his font, his deposition in the Old Bailey in January 1819 ( “my father is a tailor, and lives in Church-street, Soho” ), his marriage to Matilda Ford three months later, his bankruptcy in 1824, and his burial in the German Lutheran register on 22 April 1832. Now it has his illness, and his father’s grief, twenty months before the end.

frederick-kolbe-of-1816.v: NOT a son of Johan Gottlieb — and the second Kolbe household in Soho
frederick-kolbe-of-1816.r: RIGHT SURNAME, RIGHT PARISH, RIGHT DECADE, AND A GAP IN THE FAMILY'S OWN BAPTISM RUN EXACTLY THERE. He is not a brother. His father is GEORGE and his mother ELIZABETH, and his register batch is C72301-7 rather than the family's C15051-2 or C06236-1. HE WAS ONE CLICK FROM BEING MADE AN EIGHTH SON, and what stopped it was reading the parents' names on the transcript instead of the name, place and year in the result list. The same check threw out HENRY KOLBE, baptised at Southwark on 2 February 1800 — father Henry, mother Susannah. AND THE REJECTION TURNED OUT NOT TO BE A DEAD END. Morning Advertiser, 31 DECEMBER 1832: “LEFT HIS HOME, MONDAY, DECEMBER 10, FREDERICK KOLBE, ABOUT 16, DARK HAIR AND EYES, WITH AN IMPEDIMENT IN HIS SIGHT. Any information addressed MRS. KOLBE, NO. 18, GERRARD-STREET, SOHO, will be rewarded; if he will return, will…” — and a boy “about 16” in December 1832 is one baptised in December 1816. GERRARD STREET IS TWO STREETS FROM CHURCH STREET. THERE WERE TWO KOLBE HOUSEHOLDS IN SOHO AT ONCE, and every Soho Kolbe record on this site has to be read against that. Whether the two families were related is not known here.

marianne-kolbe.r: Aged 35 and living with her father Johan Gottlieb in Conduit Street at the 1841 census, schedule 38. Almost certainly a sister of George Augustus, who had sailed for the Cape twenty-one years earlier and never came back. FROM THE CENSUS — no baptism has been read for her. 17 SEPTEMBER 2026 — AND THE REASON IS NOW SHARPER. The eleven known children of the house leave gaps at 1808–1812 and 1814–1818, and the 1841 ages of the three women in it — rounded down to the nearest five, so born about 1802–06, 1807–11 and 1812–16 — fall in and around those gaps. THE SAME TWO GAPS THE THREE MISSING SONS MUST SIT IN. The 1841 census records no relationships, that column beginning in 1851, SO HER PLACE IN THIS FAMILY IS AN INFERENCE FROM LIVING IN THE HOUSE. The Savoy baptism register would settle it and is locked.
marianne-kolbe.tree: That she is a daughter of the house. She is in it at the 1841 census and the 1841 census does not say who anybody is to anybody.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: And what it does to Brunswick Square Brunswick Square is in Bloomsbury. It is not in Westminster and would not appear in any of these books, so they cannot disprove it. What they can do is close the gap: he is rated in Soho from 1800 to 1831, he is in the 1841 census at St George Hanover Square with Amelia A, Charlotte and Marianne Kolbe, and he dies in St George Hanover Square in 1845 . There is no window left for a Bloomsbury house. Conduit Street is in St George Hanover Square. The obituary is the odd one out. What a rate book is, and why it beat the directory. A trade directory lists the men who paid to be listed. A rate book lists everyone the parish could get money out of, every year, by street.

george-augustus-kolbe.r: HIS OBITUARY IS FOUND, eighteen days after the death: Grahamstown Journal, 19 December 1844. “DIED at his Farm, Wirtemberg, near the Orange River, December 1st, THE REV. GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE, aged 44 years, a man possessed of a most amiable temper, and of more than ordinary abilities. HE WAS THE LAST REMAINING OF EIGHT SONS OF JOHN GODLOFF KOLBE ESQ. OF BRUNSWICK-SQUARE, LONDON, has left a WIDOW AND TEN CHILDREN... he having been for many years engaged in RENDERING THEM MEDICAL ADVICE AND ASSISTANCE whenever called upon... HIS DISEASE WAS AN AFFECTION ON THE LUNGS.” EIGHT SONS, seven of them dead before December 1844 and not one in this archive. BRUNSWICK SQUARE, which is not Conduit Street and is a mile and a half from it. A MAN WHO DOCTORED A DISTRICT FOR THIRTY YEARS, where his own death notice says only “Agriculturist”. And a cause of death, after nearly a year ill. The notice also says 44 when he was 41, and ten children when this archive counts eleven living — it is the best kind of source and it is not a register. 1820 Settler — the Nautilus, Owen's party, Algoa Bay 14 Apr 1820. Married at sixteen on a sworn falsehood, AND THE ROLL CARRIES A SECOND ONE: “KOLBE, GEORGE AUGUSTUS 20. CHEMIST. W MARGARET 19”, where he was sixteen and she was sixteen. HE SAILED FROM GRAVESEND FOUR DAYS BEFORE HIS SEVENTEENTH BIRTHDAY. The two lies do not even agree — nobody “twenty-one and upwards” in January 1819 is twenty in December. OWEN'S PARTY WAS 52 PEOPLE, No. 3 on the Colonial Department list, joint-stock and recruited in London, and IT COLLAPSED IN 1821 when Thomas Owen refused to draw rations and left; his brother took over and the party dispersed. He was eighteen, with no leader, no rations and no location, and the next record of him is the Graaff-Reinet mission three years later. Preached across the Orange River. His grandson could not name him in 1915. 15 SEPTEMBER — HE WAS AN LMS MISSIONARY, AND HIS FATHER WROTE TO HIM. The South African Library at Cape Town holds MSB751, the GA KOLBE COLLECTION, donated by Dr Jean Griffiths of Somerset West in 1985: “George Augustus Kolbe, PHARMACIST, 1820 settler, MISSIONARY, married Margaret Downing” and, on a second entry, “George Augustus Kolbe, 1802–44. LMS MISSIONARY.” IT CORROBORATES A MEMORY THIS ARCHIVE PUBLISHED THE SAME MORNING AS AN INFERENCE — John Montgomery's recollection of a BUSHMAN MISSION SCHOOL AT KOOLSKOP about 1824, where Colesberg now stands. Two sources with nothing to do with each other, agreeing. THE COLLECTION IS FOUR PHOTOCOPIED PAGES CONTAINING A LETTER OF 23 AUGUST 1830 FROM JOHAN KOLBE IN LONDON TO HIS SON — the only known document connecting the tailor of Conduit Street to the settler of Colesberg. IT HAS NOW BEEN READ, AND IT DOES NOT CARRY A STREET ADDRESS. THE CATALOGUE CALLED IT A LETTER “ON HIS ORDINATION” AND THIS ARCHIVE REPEATED THE CATALOGUE; IT IS NOT. 20 SEPTEMBER 2026 — AND A SECOND ATTACHMENT CAME WITH IT. A two-page Afrikaans typescript headed “MSB 751 / [Konsep] vir DSAB / VOORLOPIGE TEKS”, initialled KS and dated 18/2/92 — A DRAFT ENTRY FOR THE DICTIONARY OF SOUTH AFRICAN BIOGRAPHY, BY DR KAREL SCHOEMAN, on the word of the National Library that holds the file: “the author, KS, would be Dr. Karel Schoeman who worked here at the National Library”. IT IS A SECONDARY WORK AND THIS ARCHIVE DOES NOT TAKE SECONDARY WORKS AS EVIDENCE — BUT IT AGREES WITH THIS ARCHIVE ON NINE POINTS REACHED BY NINE OTHER ROADS (the 1802 birth, J.G.E. Kolbe 1822–68 at Leeuberg as a commandant, Margaret Downing 1803–1867, the 1819 London marriage, the apothecary’s trade, the farm Wurthemberg, ten children, Philippolis from March 1831) AND IT IS WRONG ABOUT EXACTLY ONE THING: it calls his father A GERMAN APOTHECARY. He was a tailor, on 121 rate books, two printed masters’ lists, three Gazette notices, the census, the burial register and his other son’s sworn deposition. THE TRADE IS THE SON’S, MOVED ONE GENERATION UP. WHAT THE ENTRY ADDS, ALL OF IT UNTESTED: the GRAAFF-REINET MISSIONARY SOCIETY from about 1824, WORKING AMONG THE SLAVES of the district; acceptance as an LMS MISSION ASSISTANT ON 8 FEBRUARY 1828 and posting to BOESMANSKOOL — THE PRESENT BETHULIE — with JAMES CLARK among the SAN; a journey with MELVILL to the CALEDON VALLEY IN NOVEMBER 1828, as far as present-day Ladybrand, THE EARLIEST JOURNEY IN THE PRESENT FREE STATE OF WHICH A WRITTEN RECORD SURVIVES, and PRINTED UNDER HIS OWN NAME in the Transactions of the Missionary Society for 1829 — a second document he wrote himself, SEARCHED FOR AND NOT FOUND; PHILIPPOLIS from March 1831, alone after Melvill left in March 1832; ORDINATION ON 25 MAY 1833 BY THE FRENCH MISSIONARIES ARBOUSSET AND CASALIS; his advice behind the Berlin Missionary Society’s founding of BETHANIE in 1834; AN ACCUSATION OF ADULTERY IN 1836 with the wife of one of his congregation, agitated by H. HENDRICKS, secretary of the Griqua Council — AN INQUIRY BY THE FRENCH MISSIONARIES ACQUITTED HIM — continued opposition from T. ATKINSON, withdrawal from the station in MARCH 1837 and DISMISSAL BY THE LMS ON 19 JUNE 1837; and the farm DRIEFONTEIN near Philippolis. IT IS ALSO WRONG A SECOND TIME, AND IN ITS OWN FIRST SOURCE: it says his death notice records only eight children. THE DEATH NOTICE NAMES TEN, and this archive has read it, photographed it and published the transcription — KAB MOOC 6/9/35: 7698, signed M. Kolbe at Colesberg in January 1845. IT ALSO SETTLES THE FARM NAME. This archive had WIRTEMBERG from the obituary and KNAPDAAR from the death notice and had quietly run them into one address; “WURTHEMBERG, SOMETIMES ALSO GIVEN AS KNAPDAAR” is the statement that assumption needed. AND IT NAMES A PORTRAIT: a likeness of him AS A YOUNG MAN, in 1992 with C.J. DU PLESSIS OF RUIGTEVLEI, district Bethulie, reproduced in Olivier (1973); and a CHARLES BELL WATERCOLOUR OF A CHURCH SERVICE AT PHILIPPOLIS IN 1834 WITH KOLBE IN THE PULPIT, in the Africana Museum, Johannesburg. THIS ARCHIVE HOLDS NO LIKENESS OF ANYBODY BORN BEFORE 1850. There may be two of this man. AND HE WROTE SOMETHING ELSE, AND IT IS FINDABLE. The 1829 journal extract the DSAB cites is catalogued under the OTHER man’s name, which is why a search for Kolbe found nothing: “EXTRACTS OF THE JOURNAL OF MESSRS MELVILL AND KOLBE, ADDRESSED TO THE REV. RICHARD MILES, SUPERINTENDENT OF THE SOCIETY’S MISSIONS IN AFRICA, PHILIPPOLIS, 25 NOV. 1828”, in the Council for World Missions archive at SOAS — which is source 4 on the DSAB’s own list, two lines above source 6. An edited version dated 18 November 1828 appears in MELVILL (1829), and the journey is printed entire in KAREL SCHOEMAN (ed.), EARLY WHITE TRAVELLERS IN THE TRANSGARIEP, 1819–1840 (Protea, 2003), p. 30. LEGASSICK QUOTES HIM: on the Caledon they met people with “NO OTHER MEANS OF SUBSISTENCE THAN THE WILD ANIMALS FOUND IN THESE PARTS”. THE FIRST WORDS OF HIS THIS ARCHIVE HAS READ, AND THEY ARE ABOUT FAMINE. AND THE MAN HE ADDRESSED IT TO IS VERY PROBABLY THE MAN WHO CALLED AT HIS FATHER’S HOUSE: Richard Miles was sent to Cape Town to act as DR PHILIP’S SUBSTITUTE while Philip was in England, which puts him at the Cape in 1828 and back in London by 1830. The 1830 letter says only “Mr Miles”, so this is an identification and not a document. 20 SEPTEMBER, LATER — AND THE SOCIETY’S OWN REGISTER HAS HIM, FREE, IN EIGHT LINES. James Sibree, A REGISTER OF MISSIONARIES (LMS, 4th ed. 1923), ENTRY 278: “Was previously connected with the GRAAFF REINET MISSIONARY SOCIETY, and laboured AMONG THE SLAVES around Graaff Reinet. Was ACCEPTED PROVISIONALLY BY MR. MILES, FEB. 8, 1829, which action was CONFIRMED BY THE DIRECTORS, JULY 29, 1829. First laboured with MR. CLARK, at the BUSHMAN STATION, CALEDON RIVER. Thence proceeded to PHILIPPOLIS, arriving there, MARCH 13, 1831. On MAY 26, 1833, he was ordained by the French missionaries, Messrs. LEMUE, PELLISIER, AND ARBOUSSET. His connection was dissolved by the Directors, JUNE 19, 1837.” IT SETTLES MR MILES — the man who called at the tailor’s house in London was no messenger, HE WAS THE OFFICER WHO ACCEPTED HIM — and it explains the father’s adverb, because “provisionally” by Miles and “confirmed” by the Directors is precisely what “FULLY accepted” means. IT DISAGREES WITH THE DSAB on the year of acceptance (1829, not 1828), the day of the ordination (26 May) and the men who performed it (Lemue, Pellissier and Arbousset — no Casalis). AND IT IS WRONG ABOUT A SON. Entry 522 calls FREDERICK WILLIAM KOLBE, the Rhenish then LMS missionary of George and Paarl, “SON OF REV. G. A. KOLBE (No. 278)”, where Schoeman says he was no relation. SCHOEMAN IS RIGHT AND THE SOCIETY’S OWN REGISTER IS WRONG: the arithmetic gave it away — a birth of 3 November 1821 against John Gerson Eliezar’s 7 July 1822, EIGHT MONTHS APART — and three works settled it. The New Catholic Encyclopedia calls his son Monsignor F.C. Kolbe “the son of a WESTPHALIAN (GERMAN) PROTESTANT MISSIONARY”; S2A3 names him FRIEDRICH WILHELM KOLBE, Herero scholar, married at Cape Town in 1849 and at Okahandja by April 1850; and the DSAB had published its own entry on him in 1987. SIBREE HAS TWO KOLBES IN SOUTH AFRICA AND A COMPILER JOINED THEM. AND HIS OWN JOURNALS ARE CATALOGUED, IN LONDON. The Council for World Mission archive at SOAS, item-level: CWM/LMS/05/05/100 — “Extracts from the Journal of JOHN MELVILL AND GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE, during a tour to the north-eastwards of Philippolis, 13–22 NOV 1828”, the manuscript behind the printed extract this archive hunted all morning; /102, extracts at Philippolis 1828–1831; /106, Journal, Philippolis 1831–1834; /108, Journal, Philippolis 6 Oct 1832 – Sep 1833. SIX YEARS OF HIS LIFE IN HIS OWN WRITING, where this archive has held one sentence of his at second hand. AND THE YEAR OF THE ACCUSATION IS ONE BOX: incoming correspondence /044 (1835, which the catalogue says contains him), /046 (1836) and the 1837 file — 1836–1837 IS BOX 15. AND ONE LIKENESS IS CATALOGUED, IN SCOTLAND: University of Edinburgh, Centre for the Study of World Christianity, CSWC 60 — five photograph copies of Bell sketches of African congregations, ITEM 3 “MR. KOLBE… AT PHILIPPOLIS IN 1834”. Edinburgh calls him “a moravian missionary?”, question mark and all; HE WAS LONDON MISSIONARY SOCIETY, and this archive has his father’s letter saying so. The DSAB puts the original watercolour in Johannesburg and never mentions Scotland; Edinburgh never mentions Johannesburg.

hits.text: What was searched → Why this archive exists In 1915 a man at Barkly East filled in his own mother's death notice. Where it asked for her parents' names, he wrote: "Father: Kolbe, thinks James was christian name . Mother: Unknown ." His grandfather was George Augustus Kolbe — who married at sixteen on a sworn lie in Shoreditch, sailed on the Nautilus in 1819 as an 1820 Settler , preached across the Orange River, and named a Karoo farm after the Württemberg his own father had left. His grandmother was Margaret Downing of London.

hits.title: The Barrys
hits.text: The 1820 Settler hypothesis does not survive arithmetic. He was born 8 June 1819 . The settler fleets sailed from late 1819 and reached Algoa Bay from April 1820. He cannot have been born on that voyage. But the family does have a documented 1820 Settler — his own father-in-law, George Augustus Kolbe , who sailed on the Nautilus from Gravesend on 3 December 1819. Inferred The likeliest reading is that a true settler story attached itself to the wrong branch.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: George Augustus Kolbe was born 7 December 1802 . On 20 January 1819 he was sixteen years and six weeks old . Margaret Downing was born 23 February 1803 ; she was fifteen years and eleven months . Under Hardwicke's Marriage Act of 1753 a minor under twenty-one could not marry by licence without a parent's consent.

hits.title: Method
hits.text: The rule was written for a good reason — to stop John Barry collecting every mention of John Barry Booyzen — and it was implemented as “delete the shorter man” rather than “let the longer name go first”. So the moment anybody added George Augustus Kolbe of Wakkerstroom , George Augustus Kolbe stopped existing as far as the build was concerned. Why it is worth a section The data was never wrong. Every record, every document, every citation was intact and on disk the whole time.

hits.title: Open Questions
hits.text: The single most important unopened door: it indexes Cape (KAB) and Transvaal (TAB) estate files and death notices , which is where a death notice for Willem Hermanus Booyzen would be found. Cape Archives (KAB), Master's Office (MOOC) — one reference is already in hand: MOOC 6/9/35: 7698 (1845) , the estate of George Augustus Kolbe. That one has since been read — it is published in full, and on 20 September it caught an error in a historian’s draft that cites it as his own first source. The notice → The rest of the Master's Office holdings are still unopened.

margaret-downing.d: 2_ Nov 1867, Burgersdorp — the day illegible on the stone
margaret-downing.r: THE ANSWER WAS ON A PHOTOGRAPH THIS ARCHIVE HAS HAD ALL ALONG. The Burgersdorp monument is on the Kolbe page, and the caption quoted it as far as “ALSO HIS RELICT MARGARET DOWNING…” AND STOPPED THERE. The stone goes on: “BORN IN LONDON 23 FEBRUARY 1803 AND DIED AT BURGHERSDORP 2_ NOVEMBER 1867.” HER BIRTH IS NOW A DATE — 23 February 1803, where this archive had “c. 1804” — AND THE DEATH IS SETTLED AT 1867. Her son’s obituary of 15 April 1868 said she had died “about three months since”, which would have been January 1868; it was nearly five months, and a journalist rounding is a journalist rounding. THE DAY IS A 2 AND A DIGIT THAT WILL NOT RESOLVE at any magnification, and is not guessed. The Cape estate ran on: MOOC 13/1/253 no. 2, “DOWNING, MARGARET, WIDOW OF KOLBE, GEORGE AUGUSTUS. LIQUIDATION AND DISTRIBUTION ACCOUNT”, 1869 — and she had made a WILL OF HER OWN in 1854, MOOC 7/1/295 no. 70, ten years after she was widowed. Married at fifteen in Shoreditch, signing with a mark. Died owning a house and a farm. 20 SEPTEMBER 2026 — AND THERE IS A CERTIFICATE, IN A MUSEUM. The DSAB draft on her husband lists among its sources “ALBANY MUSEUM, GRAHAMSTAD: FOTOKOPIE VAN DIE HUWELIKSSERTIFIKAAT VAN G.A. KOLBE (1819)”. THIS ARCHIVE HOLDS THE ALLEGATION AND NOT THE MARRIAGE — the sworn statement made to get the licence, which is where the false age was sworn, and not the register entry that followed it. A photocopy of the certificate has been sitting in Grahamstown since before 1992. The same entry gives her dates as “(1803–1867)”, WHICH IS WHAT THE BURGERSDORP STONE SAYS, from a source that had not read the stone this way.

frederik-fortunatus-kolbe.r: THE SOURCE OF THE FORTUNATUS NAME across three families — and, as of 14 September 2026, A MAN WITH A HOUSEHOLD. The Settler's tenth child, born at a mission station the year his father was working the Orange River. He married ELIZABETH JOHANNA DU TOIT, and eight of their children are in the Dutch Reformed registers: baptised at COLESBERG in 1863, 1865, 1868, 1873, 1876 and 1877, at HOPETOWN in 1870, and at BETHULIE in 1881. The eldest is a GEORGE AUGUSTUS, named for the grandfather who had been dead nineteen years. THEN THE HOUSEHOLD GOES NORTH: three of those children marry or die at WAKKERSTROOM in the eastern Transvaal, four hundred miles from the font. That is the second proof of the Wakkerstroom convergence, and it does not depend on a name — it is a family moving. 17 SEPTEMBER 2026 — HE HAS A DEATH, A DISTRICT AND AN ESTATE. Pietermaritzburg estate files: “FREDERICK FORTUNABIS KOLBE, BORN 1839 KAAP PROVINSIE, DIED 23 NOVEMBER 1929 AT UTRECHT”, probate 1929 — FamilySearch 1:1:QLR2-XFJC. NINETY YEARS OLD. AND THE ESTATE NAMES HIS CHILDREN, the daughters under both surnames, which is how a daughter gets followed: George Augustus, Gabriel Stephanus, Martha Angelina, MARGARET HARRIET KOLBE VAN DER SPUY, FREDERICK FORTUNATUS, CATHARINA MARIA LOUISA KOLBE LOUW, ELIZABETH JOHANNA KOLBE PATTISON, PETRONELLA JACOBA ADRIANA KOLBE BEUKES and ADRIANA HENRIETTA JOHANNA KOLBE OOSTHUIZEN. NINE, NOT EIGHT — the note above is careful and says eight are in the REGISTERS; the ninth is not. THE FILE ITSELF IS NOT READ.

george-augustus-kolbe-of-wakkerstroom.r: THE SETTLER'S GRANDSON, CARRYING HIS NAME ENTIRE, and the man the Wakkerstroom Kolbes descend from. Baptised at Colesberg in the year of his uncle Frederick Fortunatus Barry's birth. Married MARTHA SOPHIA KLOPPER, who was seventeen, about 1885; their eldest, Maria Johanna, was born at Wakkerstroom in 1886. AND HIS STONE SETTLES THE IDENTIFICATION BEYOND ARGUMENT: “VADER — GEORGE AUGUSTUS — GEB. 29 JULIE 1863 — OORL. 28 SEPT. 1954”, which is the COLESBERG FONT DATE TO THE DAY. The 1902 POW record with residence Wakkerstroom is NOT HIS: the other George Augustus Kolbe of that town was born 2 October 1861 and was exactly forty through ten months of 1902, where this one was thirty-nine. Died at Wakkerstroom on 28 September 1954, aged 91, which counts EXACTLY from the Colesberg font: born 29 July 1863, dead 28 September 1954. He outlived two of his sons by thirty-six years.

hits.text: The care taken in the original entry — “records the burial place without claiming the camp” — was not enough, because naming the camp at all in an entry about a child who died in December 1901 makes the claim whatever the sentence says. → The 1902 prisoner of war could not be assigned to either George Augustus Kolbe of Wakkerstroom Taken back did A document read wrongly, or a conclusion drawn past what the document says. found Now it can, and the withdrawal of the morning is replaced by an answer rather than a shrug. The elder: “GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE — GEB. 2 OKTOBER 1861 — OORL. 8 NOVEMBER 1934”.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: The correction → And the prisoner of war is decided, in the other direction. At breakfast this archive gave the 1902 POW record — WO 108/368 , age 40, residence Wakkerstroom — to the man born in 1863, on the strength of the residence. By lunch it had withdrawn that, because he was thirty-nine. The stones close it: the other George Augustus Kolbe of Wakkerstroom was born 2 October 1861 , and was therefore exactly forty from October 1901 to October 1902 . The prisoner is the elder man. Published, withdrawn and reversed inside one day, and all three are on the corrections page, because a reader is owed the whole of that and not just the answer.

hits.title: Method
hits.text: The rule was written for a good reason — to stop John Barry collecting every mention of John Barry Booyzen — and it was implemented as “delete the shorter man” rather than “let the longer name go first”. So the moment anybody added George Augustus Kolbe of Wakkerstroom , George Augustus Kolbe stopped existing as far as the build was concerned. Why it is worth a section The data was never wrong. Every record, every document, every citation was intact and on disk the whole time.

hits.text: He is baptised at Colesberg on 11 October 1863 — and he dies at Wakkerstroom , in the eastern Transvaal, on 28 September 1954, aged ninety-one . The age counts exactly from the font. In between he married Martha Sophia Klopper , who was seventeen; their eldest was born at Wakkerstroom in 1886; and he was dead at ninety-one before this archive existed. A prisoner of war, and this archive nearly gave him to the wrong man. WO 108/368 , the master list of Boer prisoners numbers 1–32561, holds a George Augustus Kolbe, aged 40, nationality Transvaaler, residence Wakkerstroom, prison Natal, 1902 .

george-augustus-kolbe-of-burgersdorp.r: THE SECOND GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE OF WAKKERSTROOM, and the reason this archive had to withdraw a claim within the hour. His stone: “IN LIEFVOLLE HERINNERING AAN ONS OUERS — GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE — GEB. 2 OKTOBER 1861 — OORL. 8 NOVEMBER 1934 — EN SUSANNA MARGARETHA KOLBE — GEB. 26 OKTOBER 1861 — OORL. 28 JULIE 1940 — HULLE RUS.” BORN AT BURGERSDORP, which is where the 1820 Settler is buried and where the Settler's twin son George Augustus was born in 1836; the descent is not documented here and is not claimed. He is buried at WAKKERSTROOM although he died at Standerton, in the same cemetery as the other man of his name, TWO YEARS APART IN BIRTH AND TWENTY IN DEATH. AND THE BIRTH DATE DECIDES THE PRISONER: the 1902 POW record of WO 108/368 gives a George Augustus Kolbe of Wakkerstroom AGED 40, and a man born 2 October 1861 was forty from October 1901 to October 1902, where the other was thirty-nine all year. THE PRISONER IS THIS MAN. 17 SEPTEMBER 2026 — AND NOW HE HAS PARENTS. The last 214 images of the Burgersdorp baptism register, film 008039088, hold his font: BORN 2 OCTOBER 1861, BAPTISED 12 JANUARY 1862 AT BURGERSDORP, FATHER G. A. KOLBE, MOTHER ANNA MARIA VILJOEN — FamilySearch 1:1:6FWF-YVJT, image 685. The stone gave a date and a town and this archive wrote that the descent was not documented; THE REGISTER GIVES HIM A COUPLE. He has two younger siblings in the same book. WHETHER HIS FATHER IS THE SETTLER’S TWIN SON — the G.A. Kolbe born 23 February 1836, who would have been twenty-five — IS THE NEXT STEP AND IS NOT TAKEN HERE. 16 SEPTEMBER 2026 — THE POW ENTRY NOW HAS A FOLIO: TNA WO 108/368 FOLIO 709, the War Office list of Boer prisoners of war numbers 1–32,561, which records him as a TRANSVAALER, residence WAKKERSTROOM, and held in NATAL. He is one of SIX KOLBE MEN in that list, and the only one of the six not in the southern Free State.

The Settler’s own forenames, twice Two men called George Augustus Kolbe were taken prisoner in the same war — one at Wakkerstroom , one at Bethulie . The Wakkerstroom one was already identified on this site , from the gravestones, before this search was run: George Augustus Kolbe of Burgersdorp, born 2 October 1861 , who was forty from October 1901 to October 1902 where the other Wakkerstroom man of that name, born 29 July 1863, was thirty-nine all year. The folio number is the only thing this sweep added to him. The stones → The Bethulie man is new and unattached. No descent is claimed for him.

susanna-margaretha-swart.r: His wife, named on the Free State Dutch Reformed marriage register — he 27, residence WAKKERSTROOM — and on the Wakkerstroom stone beside him, born the same year as her husband to within three weeks. The Transvaal probate index also holds a SUSANNA MARGARETHA DOWNING KOLBE, unattached, which would make a second carrier of the London surname; this archive cannot yet say whether that is her daughter or another woman.

Two men of one name in one town, which this archive had itself written down as a warning in the same hour, in the same run of searches, and then walked straight past. anna-maria-viljoen.v: the mother of the Burgersdorp Kolbes
anna-maria-viljoen.r: A WOMAN THIS ARCHIVE DID NOT HOLD UNTIL THE LAST 214 IMAGES OF THE BURGERSDORP REGISTER WERE READ. She is named as the mother at three fonts in one book: GEORGE AUGUSTUS, born 2 October 1861, baptised 12 January 1862; ANNA JOHANNA, born 29 December 1863, baptised 28 February 1864; PETRUS JACOBUS, born 11 August 1865, baptised 8 October 1865. Her husband is entered as “G A Kolbe” at the first and “George Augustus Kolbe” at the other two. HER ELDEST SON IS THE MAN ON THE WAKKERSTROOM STONE AND THE PRISONER OF WO 108/368. Nothing else of her is known — no marriage, no parents, no death. VILJOEN IS A NAME THIS ARCHIVE ALREADY CARRIES, through Adriana Christina Viljoen, and no connection is claimed.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: Utrecht and Vryheid sit either side of Wakkerstroom on the Natal–Transvaal border. This is not three children who happened to marry in one town. It is a household that moved from the Orange River to the Natal border and stayed. And one that reaches across to the other branch. The same index holds “Anna Maria Viljoen Kolbe” with a Natal estate ( 1:1:QPHZ-23XS ) — the woman found this morning in the Burgersdorp baptism register as the mother of the other George Augustus Kolbe, the one born in 1861 and buried at Wakkerstroom. Both Kolbe households ended up in the same corner of Natal. Sixty-four Kolbe entries in that collection and this archive has read none of the files.

frederick-fortunatus-kolbe-of-colesberg.r: A CHILD OF FREDERIK FORTUNATUS KOLBE AND ELIZABETH JOHANNA DU TOIT THAT NO FONT IN THIS ARCHIVE RECORDS. Pietermaritzburg estate files — “FREDERICK FORTUNATIS KOLBE, BORN 1872 COLESBERG, DIED 10 SEPTEMBER 1944 VRYHEID”, probate 1944, FamilySearch 1:1:QPHZ-2361 — and he is named as an heir on his mother’s 1923 estate, 1:1:QLR2-5CF4. HIS BIRTH YEAR FALLS IN THE ONE GAP IN HIS PARENTS’ RUN, between Margaret Harriet at Hopetown in 1870 and Catharina Maria Louisa at Colesberg in 1873. He carries his father’s name entire, which is what a family does with a son born after two daughters. THE COLESBERG REGISTER HAS NOT BEEN CHECKED FOR HIS FONT and the estate file is not read.

petronella-jacoba-adriana-kolbe.r: SHE MARRIED A BEUKES AND DIED IN NATAL, and this archive had her file days before it knew who she was. “BEUKES, PETRONELLA JACOBA ADRIANA, BORN KOLBE, BORN IN COLESBERG”, Pietermaritzburg deceased estates — recorded here on 12 September as one of “two Kolbe-born women of Colesberg with estate files, neither in this archive”. On 14 September the relationship search gave her a father, a mother and a font, AND THE FONT SAYS COLESBERG, which is what her own estate says eighty-two years later. Seventh of the eight, and the last baptised at Colesberg. THE ESTATE IS NOT READ.

maria-johanna-kolbe.v: Maria Johanna Kolbe van der Merwe
maria-johanna-kolbe.r: HER STONE IS READ AND IT NAMES HER CHILDREN THE WAY THIS FAMILY ALWAYS DOES. “IN LIEFDEVOLLE HERINNERING AAN ONS MAMMIE — MARIA JOHANNA VAN DER MERWE (GEB. KOLBE) — 26 OKT. 1886 – 1 OKT. 1953 — Wat hy doen is wel gedaan.” And underneath, six household names: MARTZI · P.S. · JUDIE · PIETMAN · CHARL EN SUZAN. THE BIRTH IS NOW A DATE — 26 October 1886, where this archive had only the year — and THE SIX CHILDREN ARE NEW. This is the THIRD stone in this archive to list children by what they were called rather than what they were registered as: the Booyzens at Silverton, the Kolbes at Wakkerstroom, and now this. BORN AT WAKKERSTROOM AND DEAD AT WAKKERSTROOM, sixty-seven years apart, in a town her grandfather had never seen. Her 1953 estate file is the document that names the whole household: FATHER George Augustus Kolbe, MOTHER Martha Sophia Klopper, HUSBAND Charl Daniel van der Merwe. Her birthplace is entered as “Wakkerstroomn, Transvaal, Blanke Unie-burger” — the clerk's spelling, and the Union's category.

frederik-fortunatus-downing-kolbe.v: Frederik Fortunetus Daomig Kolbe, on his own marriage entry
frederik-fortunatus-downing-kolbe.r: THE MAN WHO PROVED THE CONVERGENCE. He carries BOTH of this family's Kolbe names at once — FREDERIK FORTUNATUS off his grandfather, DOWNING off a London marriage of 1819 — and a London surname has no business in the eastern Transvaal except through that wedding. Born seventy-two years after it. Married HESTER GERBINA SUSANNA JOUBERT at Volksrust at twenty-one, the clerk writing his second name as “Daomig”. Dead at Wakkerstroom on 2 November 1918, four months after his brother Daniel, which is the influenza.

hits.title: The Kolbes
hits.text: Elizabeth Johanna , baptised at Colesberg in 1876, marries John Charles Pattison there at twenty-one. In both cases the age on the marriage agrees with the font to the year. This is the second proof of the Wakkerstroom connection, and it is the better one. The first was a name: Frederik Fortunatus Downing Kolbe , born at Wakkerstroom in 1891, carrying a London surname that has no business in the eastern Transvaal except through a Shoreditch wedding of 1819. That was decisive but it was a single word on a single record. This is a household — a father, a mother, eight fonts in three towns, and three of the children turning up together at the far end. Names can be coincidence. A family moving is not.

hits.text: That was decisive but it was a single word on a single record. This is a household — a father, a mother, eight fonts in three towns, and three of the children turning up together at the far end. Names can be coincidence. A family moving is not. 1918, four months apart Daniel Jakobus Kolbe , born 3 May 1893, died 19 June 1918 at Wakkerstroom, aged 25. Frederik Fortunatus Downing Kolbe , born 1891, died 2 November 1918 at Wakkerstroom, aged 27. Two brothers, four months apart, in the year of the influenza. Their father outlived them both by thirty-six years.

angeline-kolbe.r: A WOMAN OF THIS NAME DIES AT WAKKERSTROOM IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WAR, and this archive cannot say who she is. Twenty-eight years old, female, surname Kolbe, registered at Wakkerstroom on 15 November 1900. SHE IS NOT THE VOLKSRUST CAMP GRAVE: that is a G.E. Kolbe aged 35, a different age in a different year in a different place, and the camp was barely open in November 1900. She is not on the list of Frederik Fortunatus's eight children either — too young for Martha Angelina of 1868, too old for Catharina Maria Louisa of 1873. A daughter-in-law, most likely. THE RECORD NAMES NO PARENTS, NO HUSBAND AND NO CAUSE.

HER STONE IS IN WAKKERSTROOM MAIN CEMETERY. The index this archive read gives the burial as “Volksrust, Eastvaal District Council, Mpumalanga” — and that is a DISTRICT MUNICIPALITY, not a town; Wakkerstroom lies inside it.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: The archive’s own note was careful and said “eight of their children are in the Dutch Reformed registers” — the ninth was not, and he is named for his father. The Angeline question, answered by exclusion Martha Angelina Kolbe’s record carried a warning: an Angeline Kolbe died at Wakkerstroom in 1900 , and a Martha Angeline Kolbe was buried at Volksrust in 1901 aged two months , and “neither can yet be attached to her, and this archive will not guess.” It does not have to guess now. Martha Angelina is named as an heir on her mother’s estate in 1923 and her father’s in 1929 . She was alive for both.

hits.title: The Kolbes
hits.text: Their father outlived them both by thirty-six years. Daniel's death registration carries the words G A Kolbe's son , which the index mangled into G A Kolbelsson — and that misprint is the line that ties the graves to the old man. Two women the war took, and one this archive cannot name Angeline Kolbe , aged 28, died at Wakkerstroom on 15 November 1900 . Martha Angeline Kolbe , born 9 October 1901, died 8 December 1901, buried at Volksrust — sixty days old. Volksrust held a concentration camp, and this archive records the burial place without claiming the cause, because it has read no camp register that names the child. martha-angeline-kolbe.r: HER STONE IS READ, AND IT TAKES BACK WHAT THIS ARCHIVE SAID THIS MORNING. “TER GEDACHTENIS VAN ONS GELIEFDE KLEINE — MARTHA ANGELINE KOLBE — GEBOREN 9 OCT. 1901 — OVERLEDEN 8 DEC. 1901 — HEBR. 6”, and cut across the base, the mason’s town: NEWCASTLE. IT STANDS IN WAKKERSTROOM MAIN CEMETERY, NOT AT VOLKSRUST. The index this archive read gives her burial as “Volksrust, Eastvaal District Council” — which is the DISTRICT, not the town, and Wakkerstroom lies inside it. WITH THE TOWN GOES THE CAMP: a family stone in a town churchyard, in Dutch, cut by a monumental mason twenty-five miles away in Natal, is not a camp burial, and this archive should not have gone near the word. She was sixty days old, she died in the middle of the war, and that is all that can be said. She carries the name of her great-aunt Martha Angelina, baptised at Colesberg in 1868.

hits.text: The archive’s own note was careful and said “eight of their children are in the Dutch Reformed registers” — the ninth was not, and he is named for his father. The Angeline question, answered by exclusion Martha Angelina Kolbe’s record carried a warning: an Angeline Kolbe died at Wakkerstroom in 1900 , and a Martha Angeline Kolbe was buried at Volksrust in 1901 aged two months , and “neither can yet be attached to her, and this archive will not guess.” It does not have to guess now. Martha Angelina is named as an heir on her mother’s estate in 1923 and her father’s in 1929 . She was alive for both.

hits.title: The Kolbes
hits.text: Daniel's death registration carries the words G A Kolbe's son , which the index mangled into G A Kolbelsson — and that misprint is the line that ties the graves to the old man. Two women the war took, and one this archive cannot name Angeline Kolbe , aged 28, died at Wakkerstroom on 15 November 1900 . Martha Angeline Kolbe , born 9 October 1901, died 8 December 1901, buried at Volksrust — sixty days old. Volksrust held a concentration camp, and this archive records the burial place without claiming the cause, because it has read no camp register that names the child. Angeline is not the camp grave NAAIRS holds — that is a G.E. Kolbe, aged 35 , a different age in a different year in a different town.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: The official record at the end of his life calls him simply an agriculturist , and he died on his own farm. Those are not contradictions — they are a life in sequence — but the archive should stop leading with "missionary". Ten children, and one who is missing The notice names ten. Keetor Peter Benjamin Kolbe , whom the tree gives a birth in 1840, is not among them — nor among the ten in his mother's 1867 notice. He died young, or he does not belong in this family. Julia Kolbe , whom MyHeritage flags as born two years after her father's death, is likewise absent, as she must be.

hits.text: The one death notice where line 3 works Found found TAB MHG 2945/44, read at full resolution off the film. Anna Johanna Maria Booyzen, born Pretorius, died Forest Hill 26 February 1944, aged 37. The parents line — blank or evasive on all four earlier notices in this archive — is filled in completely: Petrus Jacobus Pretorius and Margareth Wilhelmina Elizabeth Pretorius, both at 96 James Street, Germiston. The form did not change. The person filling it in did. Her husband signed it, and her parents were alive and reachable. hits.title: What changed
hits.text: DOROTHEA REGINA AND RUBEN JACOBUS JOSUAH ARE NOT ON IT, and this archive had both as children “named on the 1915 death notice”. They are grandchildren: a Dorothea Regina baptised at Slang River in 1892 and a Ruben Jacobus Hosea at Dordrecht in 1888, both to Henry Nicholas Barry and Anna Johanna Maria Schoeman. The page also gives Margaretha Kolbe's death as 2 AUGUST 1912, where this archive had only the year. And it says the marriage took place at “Burghersdorp (probably)” — a son of the house, writing in English with a solicitor's help, who did not know where his parents married and put it in brackets.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: The tree is wrong three times over. Boomkweker Not a miner, and not yet a railwayman. In 1924 George grew trees. A wholly new occupation for him — and by 1947 he was a clerk on the South African Railways . Both were living at Evaton — where Anna's grandmother Anna Johanna Maria Schoeman had died the year before. The whole connection had moved north together. 1947 · The death registration, and a garbled memory vindicated Entry 10,899 , Johannesburg, registered 12 December 1947 — a second document, distinct from the death notice.

tersia-booyzen.r: Recorded the name-change and Anglo-Boer War account on the MyHeritage tree, as told to her by her father. It is FAMILY TESTIMONY AND NOT FROM A DOCUMENT — which is exactly why this archive quotes it in full and then tests it against the Cape Rebel rolls and the surname distribution, rather than repeating it.

hits.title: The Booyzen Archive
hits.text: It carries seven separate claims. None of them has yet been proved. Two are already in trouble, and three now have strong circumstantial support that did not exist before this archive was built.

hits.title: Disputed
hits.text: Documented He was not shot by anybody. The death registration → Inferred Three readings survive, and the archive does not choose between them: The generations are miscounted. Tersia Booyzen was counting from herself, not from the current researcher. Her "great great grandfather" may be a man this archive has not identified. "Shot and killed" is not an execution. It may mean killed in action, or shot during a farm clearance — neither of which would appear on the treason lists.

hits.title: The documents
hits.text: This archive has not seen the medal, the ABO application, or Schroeder's signature. It is strong secondary evidence, and the prisoner number is what ties it to the register rather than to a name alone. The family's own war testimony now has something to be tested against. This archive has quoted Tersia Booyzen's account in full for the whole project and measured it only against surname distributions and rebel district figures, because there was no record. There is one now: a policeman of Pretoria who was at Talana in the first week of the war, wounded at Wagon Hill, present at Spion Kop and at the ZARPs' last stand, taken at Tolosberg with forty-one others and two guns, and shipped to India.

The full account → Documented That a change happened is on the record twice over. MyHeritage carries "Former name: Booysen" as a formal Name Change fact on Willem Hermanus "William Henry" Booyzen (1851–1905) — and, far better, both spellings appear on a single sheet of paper in September 1905 .
